lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: steps that require an adult

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 3: Kitchen Care and Food Safety
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice steps that require an adult. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A trusted adult picks one simple, real food or drink the household is actually planning to make, such as scrambled eggs, grilled cheese, or a smoothie, and writes out every step from start to finish.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult reviews the full step list with the learner before any step is prepared and personally performs or directly supervises every step involving heat, a stove or oven, a sharp blade, or a small appliance.
The learner never turns on a stove, oven, or appliance, and never handles a sharp blade, even to test their sort; sorting a step correctly is what earns credit, not performing it.
If the household's real recipe includes a step the learner is unsure about, the correct move is to mark it 'ask the adult' rather than guess, and asking counts as a correct response.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real recipe or kitchen access is available, the learner instead reads a printed or written step list for a common simple food, such as instructions for making toast with jam or a basic fruit salad, sorts each step into the same three categories, and writes the specific hazard reasoning for every adult-only step without needing an actual kitchen or ingredients.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app to write the sorted list
adult-or-local: the actual kitchen where the food will be made

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Describe a specific time you remember an adult-only kitchen step being done, and explain what could have gone wrong if a kid had tried that step without an adult.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Hazard-based sorting accuracy: Every step is sorted, and every adult-only step names a specific hazard (heat, blade, appliance, or chemical). | Division-of-labor reasoning: The plan names who does each step and ties the reasoning back to the specific hazard identified earlier. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner sort the steps for a second, different real food or drink the household plans to make later in the week, then compare in writing which of the two tasks had more adult-only steps and why.

resources.title: steps that require an adult worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A trusted adult picks one simple, real food or drink the household is actually planning to make, such as scrambled eggs, grilled cheese, or a smoothie, and writes out every step from start to finish.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact steps that require an adult decision or action.
Model move 2: Before sorting anything, read through the whole step list with your adult once, start to finish.
Model move 3: Go through the step list one step at a time with your adult and sort each one into 'alone,' 'next to an adult,' or 'adult only,' saying your reason out loud before writing it down.

Model check: Hazard-based sorting accuracy: Every step is sorted, and every adult-only step names a specific hazard (heat, blade, appliance, or chemical). | Division-of-labor reasoning: The plan names who does each step and ties the reasoning back to the specific hazard identified earlier.

2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-model-card.

resources.title: steps that require an adult coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult picks one simple, real food or drink the household is actually planning to make, such as scrambled eggs, grilled cheese, or a smoothie, and writes out every step from start to finish.
Coach direction: Before sorting anything, read through the whole step list with your adult once, start to finish.
Learner prompt: Name one step in the list that you are already sure you can do completely by yourself.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: steps that require an adult complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Go through the step list one step at a time with your adult and sort each one into 'alone,' 'next to an adult,' or 'adult only,' saying your reason out loud before writing it down.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I gave every single step in the list one of the three sorting labels.
Response 2 (t2-p2): For every 'adult only' step, I named the specific hazard: heat, a sharp blade, an appliance, or a cleaning chemical.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My adult confirmed or corrected each of my sorting decisions before we moved to the next step.

Equal-access rule: If no real recipe or kitchen access is available, the learner instead reads a printed or written step list for a common simple food, such as instructions for making toast with jam or a basic fruit salad, sorts each step into the same three categories, and writes the specific hazard reasoning for every adult-only step without needing an actual kitchen or ingredients.

resources.title: steps that require an adult minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe a specific time you remember an adult-only kitchen step being done, and explain what could have gone wrong if a kid had tried that step without an adult.

Success checks: Hazard-based sorting accuracy: Every step is sorted, and every adult-only step names a specific hazard (heat, blade, appliance, or chemical). | Division-of-labor reasoning: The plan names who does each step and ties the reasoning back to the specific hazard identified earlier.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: steps that require an adult supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional steps that require an adult condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Hazard-based sorting accuracy: Every step is sorted, and every adult-only step names a specific hazard (heat, blade, appliance, or chemical). | Division-of-labor reasoning: The plan names who does each step and ties the reasoning back to the specific hazard identified earlier..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: steps that require an adult — permitted real-life route

steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Go through the step list one step at a time with your adult and sort each one into 'alone,' 'next to an adult,' or 'adult only,' saying your reason out loud before writing it down.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record; only the household-authorized guardian attests that the named physical action occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
